mainTopic: Writing a גט on an animal (רבי יוסי הגלילי vs. רבנן), and trees as סוכה walls that must withstand a normal wind
overview: This amud opens with the closing line of an earlier discussion: a living animal used as a סוכה wall counts as a מחיצה made by a person. The גמרא then quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says a גט may not be written on an animal. His source is a ברייתא: "וכתב לה" allows any material, but "ספר" limits it to things that, like a scroll, are not alive and are not food. רבנן read "ספר" as ספירת דברים, a written account, so for them a גט may be written on anything. The גמרא then works out how each side uses "וכתב", "ספר כריתות" and the longer form "כריתות". These sources teach that money cannot divorce and that a גט must fully cut the bond. A new משנה rules that trees can serve as the walls of a סוכה. רב אחא בר יעקב says a wall that cannot stand in a normal wind is not a wall. The גמרא reconciles this rule with the משנה and with two other sources by saying the trees were hard and their branches tied down. It ends with a challenge from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The partition counts as made by a person
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous discussion: the מחיצה in question is considered made by a person, so it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a partition made by a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion about an animal used as a wall of a סוכה. It concludes that this מחיצה counts as made by a human being, so it is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא was discussing an animal wall that stands only because of רוח (air or wind), since a partition held up by רוח might not count. This line settles the point: as רש"י explains, this רוח was put there by a person, so it counts as a man-made wall. With that settled, the גמרא can move on to the next part of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Made by human hands, set up by a person

phrases.english: Behold, it is made by human hands.
phrases.notes: End of the previous discussion about an animal used as a סוכה wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came on the previous amud about an animal as a partition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The partition is treated as man-made and therefore valid.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: no גט written on an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא: in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי, a גט may not be written on an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said in the ברייתא: In the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי they said: one may also not write a גט on it, meaning on an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes a new line from it. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask for the reason behind this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was discussing an animal used as a wall of a סוכה. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds a second rule about animals: you cannot write a גט on one. The word "אף" ("also") shows that he is adding a further restriction about animals.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the formula for quoting an earlier source in order to discuss it

steps.confusionAlert: "עליו" ("on it") means on the animal from the ברייתא's case, not on the סוכה.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can look at it closely.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili they said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵין כּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: Also, one may not write bills of divorce for women on it (the animal).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר. מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to analyze a new line of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a גט may not be written on a living animal.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source and logic behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי הגלילי says a גט cannot be written on an animal. It is setting up a source from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know which verse or logic leads to this rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for forbidding a גט written on a living creature.

steps.title: The verse includes any material for a bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the verse: "ספר" alone would mean only a scroll, but "וכתב לה" includes writing a גט on any material.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: "ספר" would teach me only a scroll. How do we know to include anything? The verse says "וכתב לה", "and he shall write for her", meaning on anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with a ברייתא. First, the ברייתא shows that a גט can be written on almost any material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading only the word "ספר", you might think a גט must be written on a scroll. The words "וכתב לה" widen this to any surface. This sets up the next step, where the ברייתא will ask why "ספר" is written at all.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know to include?

phrases.english: As it is taught: "A scroll". I would know only a scroll.
From where do we know to include any object?
The verse says: "And he shall write for her," on anything at all.
phrases.notes: Writing in any form is what counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 3 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First stage: "וכתב לה" includes any material for a גט.

steps.title: The word scroll excludes living things and food
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that "ספר" limits the materials: like a scroll, the material must not be alive and must not be food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say "ספר"? To teach you: just as a scroll is not alive and is not food, so too a גט may be written on anything that is not alive and is not food.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the verse says "ספר" if any material is allowed. It answers that "ספר" sets the limits: no living things and no food. This is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse first widens the rule ("וכתב לה", any material) and then narrows it with a model ("ספר"). Whatever is like a scroll, meaning not alive and not food, is allowed. Since an animal is alive, a גט cannot be written on it, which is exactly רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "Just as… so too": a comparison that builds a category from a model

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, "וכתב לה" allows any material, but "ספר" limits it to things that, like a scroll, are not alive and not food. So a גט on an animal is invalid.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "scroll"?
To tell you: just as a scroll

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֶל,
phrases.english: is something that is not alive and is not food,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֶל.
phrases.english: so too, any object that is not alive and is not food.
phrases.notes: So a living animal is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's derivation by explaining what the word "ספר" adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ספר" limits a גט to materials that, like a scroll, are not alive and not food. That is why an animal is excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the full source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling and sets up the question of how רבנן, who disagree, read the same word.

steps.title: How do רבנן read the word ספר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבנן, who allow a גט on anything, deal with the word "ספר".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבנן deal with this verse, since they permit a גט even on an animal or on food. It is setting up their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי. So they must explain what the word "ספר" teaches if it does not limit the writing materials.

keyTerms.meaning: "And the Rabbis?": how do they explain this?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? (How do they explain the verse?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading to the opposing view of רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבנן read "ספר" without limiting the materials of a גט.

steps.title: For רבנן, ספר means a written account of the matter
steps.stepSummary: רבנן answer: if the verse had said "בספר", it would limit the material. Since it says "ספר", it means a written account of the matters (ספירת דברים), not a type of surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse had written "בספר", "in a scroll", it would be as you said. Now that it says "ספר", it only comes to teach a telling of the matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer of רבנן. The word "ספר" here means "a written telling of the matter", so it says nothing about what the גט is written on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן focus on the wording. "בספר" ("in a scroll") would describe the surface, but plain "ספר" connects to the root ס-פ-ר, "to tell or recount". So the verse means the גט must contain a written statement of the divorce, and any surface is allowed, even a living thing or food.

keyTerms.meaning: A telling or account of the matters

steps.whatToRemember: The argument depends on one small letter. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads "ספר" as the writing surface (a scroll), so living things and food are excluded. רבנן read "ספר" as ספירת דברים, a written account, so a גט may be written on anything.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of ספר. For רבי יוסי הגלילי it means a physical scroll. For רבנן it comes from "לספר", to tell, and refers to the content of the גט, not the material.

phrases.english: If it had written "in a scroll", it would be as you said.
Now that it is written "sefer",
it comes merely to teach a telling of the matters.
phrases.notes: The word just means a written account of the divorce; it doesn't limit what you write it on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by reinterpreting the word that רבי יוסי הגלילי relied on in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plain "ספר" (not "בספר") means a written account of the matters. It places no limit on the writing surface.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "ספר" limits a גט to a scroll-like material that is not alive and not food.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבנן, "ספר" means ספירת דברים, a written account, so any material is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a single letter ("ב") can separate two readings of a verse, and it explains why רבנן allow a גט on a living creature or on food.

steps.title: What do רבנן learn from the word וכתב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with the word "וכתב", since they don't use it to allow a גט on any material the way רבי יוסי הגלילי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: what do they learn from this word "וכתב"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבנן learn from the word "וכתב". This sets up the next step, where it answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, the ברייתא used "וכתב לה" to include any writing surface. רבנן already allow a גט on anything, because for them "ספר" does not limit the material. So they don't need "וכתב" to include materials, and the גמרא wants to know what that word teaches them.

keyTerms.meaning: they expound / they learn out (from a verse)
"and he shall write" (from the verse about a גט)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: this word "and he shall write"
phrases.notes: This is the same word from step 4, the one used to include anything you can write on.

phrases.english: what do they learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how רבנן read "ספר", the גמרא now asks about the other word, "וכתב".
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבנן learn from the word "וכתב".

steps.title: Divorce is only by writing, not by money
steps.stepSummary: רבנן use "וכתב" to teach that a woman is divorced only through a written document and not through money. Without it, we might have compared divorce to קידושין, which can be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to teach that she is divorced through writing, and she is not divorced through money. You might have thought: since leaving a marriage is compared to entering a marriage, then just as entering is done with money, leaving can also be done with money. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן use "וכתב" to teach that a גט must be written, and that a woman cannot be divorced by giving her money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah connects leaving a marriage (יציאה) with entering a marriage (הויה). Because of that connection, you might have thought divorce works with money, just as קידושין does. The word "וכתב" blocks that idea: divorce works only through writing.

keyTerms.meaning: was compared (a הקש, a link the Torah makes between two topics)
it teaches us (that the first idea is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of "writing" here. In step 4, "וכתב" was about which materials a גט can be written on. Here, for רבנן, it means that a written document is required at all, as opposed to money.

phrases.english: That word is needed by them
to teach that she is divorced through writing
and she is not divorced through money.
It could have entered your mind to say:
since leaving a marriage is compared to entering a marriage,
phrases.notes: The verse says "ויצאה... והיתה", linking divorce with marriage.

phrases.english: just as entering a marriage can be done with money,
so too leaving it could be done with money.
So the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use "וכתב" to exclude divorce through money, which you might otherwise have allowed because of the הקש between יציאה and הויה.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn that money cannot divorce?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי already used "וכתב" to include all materials. So where does he learn that divorce cannot be done with money?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי, where does he get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי הגלילי and asks for his source that money cannot divorce. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי used "וכתב" for a different lesson, to include any material. Surely he also agrees that money cannot divorce. So he needs some other source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: idea / rule (here, the rule that money cannot divorce)
from where does he get it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
where does he get this rule from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the source of רבנן is known, the גמרא asks the same question for the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source that divorce cannot be done with money.

steps.title: Only a document severs her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from "ספר כריתות" that only a written document cuts off the marriage, and nothing else does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "a document of severance": a document cuts her off, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from "ספר כריתות" that only a written document ends the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the phrase as meaning that the document is what does the cutting. That excludes every other method, including money. So he gets the same rule as רבנן, just from a different word.

keyTerms.meaning: "document of severance", the Torah's name for a גט

phrases.english: He derives it from "a document of severance."
A document cuts her off,
and nothing else cuts her off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From "ספר כריתות": only a document severs the marriage, so money does not.

steps.title: What do רבנן do with ספר כריתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבנן learn from "ספר כריתות", since they learned the no-money rule from "וכתב".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side (רבנן)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with the words "ספר כריתות". This one-word question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן already got the no-money rule from "וכתב". So "ספר כריתות" must teach them something else, and the גמרא asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other side? (what does the other opinion do with this verse?)

phrases.english: And the other side (the Rabbis)?
phrases.notes: Asks what רבנן learn from "ספר כריתות".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the source used in step 11 back to רבנן.

steps.title: A גט must fully cut the bond between them
steps.stepSummary: רבנן use "ספר כריתות" to teach that a גט must completely cut the tie between husband and wife. A ברייתא shows this: a condition that binds her forever is not a valid divorce, but a condition limited to thirty days is.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed to teach that a גט must be something that cuts everything between him and her. As a ברייתא teaches: if he says, "Here is your גט on condition that you never drink wine," or "on condition that you never go to your father's house," this is not severance. If the condition is for thirty days, this is severance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן learn from "ספר כריתות" that a גט must make a full and final break between husband and wife. It brings a ברייתא as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that lasts forever keeps the husband's control over his ex-wife's life, so the bond is never fully cut and the גט is not valid. A condition with an end date, such as thirty days, does allow a full break once it is over, so that גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: a complete cutting off / full severance

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a גט with a permanent condition is not valid, because the divorce must be a complete break.

phrases.english: That phrase is needed by him
to teach that it must be something that cuts everything between him and her.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Here is your גט
on condition that you do not drink wine,"
or "on condition that you do not go
to your father's house, ever":
this is not severance.
If it is for thirty days,
this is severance.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְדָבָר הַכּוֹרֵת בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use "ספר כריתות" to require total severance, which rules out a גט with a permanent condition.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn the total-severance rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns that a גט must fully cut the bond, since he used "ספר כריתות" for the no-money rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side (רבי יוסי הגלילי)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the full-severance rule. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ספר כריתות" is already used up for him as the source that money cannot divorce. So he needs some other source for the rule against permanent conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: severance (the word whose form will be examined next)

phrases.english: And the other side (Rabbi Yosei HaGelili)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the lesson of step 13 back to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source for the requirement of total severance.

steps.title: The longer word teaches a second lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the total-severance rule from the fact that the Torah wrote the longer word "כריתות" instead of the shorter "כרת".
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the change from "כרת" to "כריתות".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns full severance from the extra letters in the word "כריתות".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written the short form "כרת". The longer form "כריתות" suggests two lessons. One is that only a document divorces, and the other is that the break must be complete.

keyTerms.meaning: the shorter form of the word for cutting

phrases.english: He derives it from "karet" being written as "keritut".
phrases.notes: The longer word adds a second lesson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The longer word "כריתות" adds the lesson of total severance.

steps.title: Why don't רבנן learn from the longer word?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבנן don't use the extra letters of "כריתות" to learn something as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side (רבנן)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with the longer form "כריתות". This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra letters teach something, רבנן should also have to learn something from them. The גמרא checks why they don't.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other side? (here referring to רבנן)

phrases.english: And the other side (the Rabbis)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the derivation in step 15 from the side of רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבנן do with the change from "כרת" to "כריתות".

steps.title: רבנן don't learn from the longer word
steps.stepSummary: רבנן do not learn anything from the change between "כרת" and "כריתות". This closes the cycle of sources for both opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not learn anything from "כרת" versus "כריתות".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן simply do not treat the longer word as teaching anything extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, "כריתות" is just the normal way to say the word, so the extra letters carry no message. This finishes the picture: both sides use every phrase in the verse, just in different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not expound (they learn nothing from it)

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: "ספר" means an account of the matters, so any material is fine. "וכתב" teaches that money cannot divorce. "ספר כריתות" teaches total severance. רבי יוסי הגלילי: "ספר" limits the material (it cannot be alive and cannot be food). "וכתב" includes all other materials. "ספר כריתות" teaches that money cannot divorce. The longer word "כריתות" teaches total severance.

phrases.english: They do not learn anything from "karet" versus "keritut".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 and closes the sequence of derivations.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן do not learn anything from the longer form of the word.

steps.title: Trees can serve as the walls of a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סוכה built between trees, with the trees acting as its walls, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone builds his סוכה between trees, and the trees are its walls, the סוכה is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that trees can count as the walls of a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The walls of a סוכה do not have to be built by a person. Something that grows naturally, like a tree, can also count as a wall.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who makes his sukkah between the trees
and the trees are walls for it —
it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, after the previous discussion of כריתות ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trees may serve as the walls of a כשרה סוכה.

steps.title: A wall that cannot withstand a normal wind is not a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rules that a מחיצה which cannot stand up to a normal wind does not count as a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Any wall that cannot hold steady in a normal, everyday wind is not a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule about walls from רב אחא בר יעקב. This rule is setting up the challenge from our משנה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall has to be stable. If an ordinary wind blows it back and forth, it does not count as a מחיצה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who states this rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about stable walls applies to every מחיצה in הלכה, not only to a סוכה.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Any partition that is not able
to stand in a normal wind —
is not a partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a general rule about walls that will be tested against the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partition that cannot withstand a normal wind is not a valid partition.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: trees sway in the wind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that allows trees as walls, and objects that trees move back and forth in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If someone builds his סוכה between trees, and the trees are its walls, it is kosher. But the trees sway back and forth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב using our משנה. Trees sway in the wind, yet the משנה still calls them valid walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אחא בר יעקב, a swaying wall is not a wall. Trees sway, so the משנה seems to contradict his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes back and forth (it sways)

phrases.english: We learned:
One who makes his sukkah between the trees
and the trees are walls for it — it is kosher.
But it sways back and forth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to attack the rule of רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב אחא בר יעקב that a swaying wall is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees sway in the wind, yet the משנה accepts them as walls.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about hard, sturdy trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה refers to thick, hard trees that do not sway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Hard trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The משנה means strong trees that stay still in the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick trees do not move in a normal wind, so they meet the rule of רב אחא בר יעקב. There is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here?

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing —
with hard ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to include all trees, even ones that sway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers only to hard trees that do not sway.

steps.title: But the leaves and branches still move
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even on a hard tree, the leaves and branches sway in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are its branches and leaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The trunk may be hard, but the leaves and branches still move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leafy part forms part of the wall, it is a swaying מחיצה. Then the סוכה should be invalid under the rule of רב אחא בר יעקב.

phrases.english: But there is its foliage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה refers to hard trees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a hard tree has leafy branches that sway, so the wall still moves.

steps.title: The branches were tied down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the person tied the foliage tight with palm leaves and laurel so that it does not move.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fixed it with hard palm leaves and laurel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the leafy branches were tied down and filled in. Now they do not sway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the foliage is tied firmly, the whole wall is stable. It then meets the rule of רב אחא בר יעקב.

phrases.english: That he made it (firm) with palm leaves and laurel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzMaskana: The foliage was tied tight, so the wall is stable.

steps.title: If so, why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the trees are hard and tied down, the ruling is obvious, so why does the משנה state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why the משנה needs to teach this at all. A stable, tied-down wall is obviously valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the last two answers, the case looks too simple to need a משנה. The גמרא looks for the new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious!)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משנה, given the answer of step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A firm, tied wall is obviously valid, so the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: No גזירה because of using a tree on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that we do not make a גזירה forbidding tree walls out of fear that a person will use the tree on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: Let us make a גזירה, in case he comes to use the tree on שבת. So the משנה teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point of the משנה. We might have banned tree walls because of a שבת concern, and the משנה tells us there is no such ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל forbade using a tree on שבת. We might have feared that a person sitting in the סוכה would lean on or use the tree. The משנה rules that we do not make that גזירה, so the tree wall is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
To use a tree (forbidden on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: Tree walls are valid only if they do not sway in a normal wind: hard trunks, with the foliage tied down. The משנה adds that we do not ban them out of fear of using the tree on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The final answer does not change the wall rule of רב אחא בר יעקב. It only explains what new point the משנה teaches: there is no גזירה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us decree, lest he come
to make use of the tree,
so it teaches us (that we do not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, explaining the new point the משנה teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would make a גזירה against tree walls because of using the tree on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה is made; the tree walls are valid.

steps.title: Proof from a tree or reed fence counting as a corner post at a well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that a swaying partition is valid. It cites the case of a tree or a fence of reeds that can count as a דיומד (corner post) around a well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if there was a tree there, or a stone fence, or a partition of reeds, it is judged like a corner post.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to show that a partition that moves in the wind can still count as a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, people may draw water from a well if it is surrounded by special corner posts called דיומדין. This source says a tree or a fence of reeds can take the place of such a post. Reeds and tree branches sway in the wind, so it seems a moving partition still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an opening that brings a source as a proof
A double corner post, used to enclose the area around a well (פסי ביראות)
Is judged as / has the legal status of

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If there was a tree there
phrases.notes: At the corner of the area around a well

phrases.english: or a fence, or a partition of reeds —
it is judged as a corner post!
phrases.notes: Reeds and trees sway in the wind, yet they still count.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה שָׁם אִילָן אוֹ גָּדֵר אוֹ מְחִיצַת הַקָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new outside source on the same question of swaying partitions.
steps.raayaObject: A partition that sways in the wind is a valid partition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling on פסי ביראות that a tree or reed partition counts as a דיומד.

steps.title: The reeds were tied down too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In that case too, the partition was tied tight with palm leaves and laurel, so it did not sway.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is because he made it firm with palm leaves and laurel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by giving the same answer it used before: the partition was tied so it would not move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the reeds or tree actually move in the wind. By saying they were tied down with הוצא ודפנא, the גמרא shows the source is talking about a partition that does not sway. So it proves nothing about moving partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: There too: the same answer applies to that case
Palm leaves and laurel, used to tie branches tight
He made it / set it up

phrases.english: There too,
it is because he made it firm with palm leaves and laurel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּעָבֵיד לֵיהּ בְּהוּצָא וְדַפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 26.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the reeds or tree sway. They were actually tied tight, so the case says nothing about moving partitions.

steps.title: Proof from carrying under a tree whose branches reach the ground
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a tree's branches hang down to within three טפחים of the ground, one may carry under it. Yet branches sway in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a tree whose branches cover the ground — if its foliage is not three handbreadths above the ground, one may carry beneath it. Why? Doesn't it sway back and forth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source: the branches of a tree are treated as walls for carrying, even though branches move in the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches less than three טפחים from the ground are treated as if they touch the ground (the rule of לבוד). So the tree forms a kind of room, and one may carry inside it. The גמרא asks how this can be, since the branches sway. That suggests a swaying wall is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Covers over / hangs down like a canopy
Three handbreadths; a gap smaller than this is treated as closed (לבוד)
Goes and comes: sways back and forth

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A tree that covers over the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין נוֹפוֹ גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: if its foliage is not high off the ground
three handbreadths —
one may carry beneath it.
Why? Doesn't it sway back and forth?
phrases.notes: This question is what turns the ברייתא into a proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִילָן הַמֵּיסֵךְ עַל הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a second source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: A partition that sways in the wind is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing carrying under a tree whose branches reach near the ground.

steps.title: The tree branches were tied down too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof the same way: the branches were tied tight with palm leaves and laurel.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where he made it firm with palm leaves and laurel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again pushes away the proof by saying the branches were tied so they would not move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the branches are tied down, they no longer sway. So the ברייתא is about a steady wall, not a moving one. The question of swaying partitions stays unproven.

phrases.english: There too,
it is where he made it firm with palm leaves and laurel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, דְּעָבֵיד לֵיהּ בְּהוּצָא וְדַפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the tree whose branches reach the ground.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the branches sway. They were tied tight, so they do not move.

steps.title: If the tree is a full wall, why limit carrying under it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the answer of step 29. If the branches were tied down to form a real wall, one should be able to carry in the whole area. Yet רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits carrying there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let one carry in all of it! Why then did רב הונא son of רב יהושע say: one may not carry in it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. Saying the branches were tied down seems to clash with a known limit from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. This passage ends in the middle of his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tied branches make a true private area, there should be no limit on carrying inside. But רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says there is a restriction. So the answer "he tied it down" seems to prove too much. His full statement continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your answer is true
Let one carry in all of it
An אמורא whose ruling limits carrying under the tree

steps.confusionAlert: The source text stops in the middle of רב הונא's sentence ("אין מטלטלין בו"). His statement continues with a limit, not a full ban. Do not read it as "one may not carry there at all."

phrases.english: If so, let one carry in all of it!

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Why then did Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua say:
One may not carry in it
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נִיטַּלְטֵל בְּכוּלֵּיהּ! אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the tree's branches were tied down with הוצא ודפנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tied-down tree should be a full private area with no limit on carrying. But רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע places a limit on carrying under it, so the answer seems wrong.
